feedback.problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=2(t+1),\,y=4{t}^{2},\,-\infty <t<\infty .
$$

Determine the value of $t$ at which the tangent to the curve is horizontal.
feedback.worked_solution:
The slope $m$ of a tangent line to a curve defined parametrically is given by

$$
m=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

The tangent line is horizontal if ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${x}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2,\,{y}^{′}(t)=8t.
$$

Solving ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
8t=0\,⟹\,t=0.
$$

Note that ${x}^{′}(0)=2\ne 0.$ Therefore, we conclude that when $t=0,$ the tangent to the curve is horizontal.
